SELECTED_INDEX: 4  
CONFIDENCE: 0.25  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows typical bands of a small aliphatic alcohol with an amine.  
• Broad band 3333 cm⁻¹ (width ≈46 cm⁻¹) is characteristic of an H-bonded O–H stretch, matching the hydroxyl present in CN(C)CCO (2-dimethylamino-ethanol).  
• Strong C–H stretches at 2873–2956 cm⁻¹ and CH₂/CH₃ bending at 1462 cm⁻¹ fit the three alkyl groups in this molecule.  
• C–O stretches of aliphatic alcohols appear near 1050–1150 cm⁻¹; peaks at 1062 and 1133 cm⁻¹ correspond well.  
• Additional medium peaks around 775–800 cm⁻¹ and 957 cm⁻¹ are consistent with C–C and C–N vibrations found in dialkylamino alcohols.  
Among the ten candidates, only molecule 4 simultaneously contains an O–H group and tertiary amine, matching the observed OH stretch and the overall simple aliphatic pattern; no other candidate offers this combination without introducing strong bands (e.g., C=O, Si–Cl, S–S, large ring) that are absent in the experimental spectrum.
